question: Tá istá termoska udrží čaj horúci a limonádu studenú. Čo je medzi jej dvoma stenami, čo bráni teplu prejsť von či dnu?
source_excerpt: double-walled vessel with the air evacuated from the space between the walls, drastically reducing heat transfer

extra.why_interesting: Players use a thermos all the time and tend to picture some special insulating material inside. The answer is that the gap holds nothing at all, and that emptiness is why the same flask works for both hot tea and cold lemonade.
extra.verification_notes: A vacuum flask's double walls enclose an evacuated space that blocks conduction and convection, so 'vacuum' is correct (https://www.scienceabc.com/innovation/thermos-flask-keep-hot-things-hot-cold-things-cold.html).

explanation: Medzi stenami je takmer prázdny priestor bez vzduchu, a kde nie je vzduch, teplo nemá ako prúdiť ani sa vedením šíriť. Termosku pôvodne vymyslel škótsky vedec James Dewar na chladenie plynov v laboratóriu, nie na čaj.

question: Turistické značky na Slovensku majú štyri farby. Ktorou farbou sú značené hlavné hrebeňové trasy, napríklad Cesta hrdinov SNP z Dukly až na Devín?
source_excerpt: long-distance hiking route that runs from Dukla Pass in the northeast to Devín Castle on the western border... with the red waymark

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak has walked past these painted stripes on trees but few have wondered whether the colours mean anything. Players can reason it out: the most important, longest route gets the most striking colour.
extra.verification_notes: The SNP Heroes Trail from Dukla to Devín is marked red, and red is the colour for main ridge routes in the Slovak system (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNP_Heroes_Trail).

explanation: Červená patrí najdôležitejším diaľkovým a hrebeňovým trasám, modrá a zelená ostatným dlhším chodníkom a žltá kratším spojkám. Po červenej sa dá prejsť takmer celé Slovensko, asi 770 kilometrov.
